groups.title: Integrated supplements and short pronominal NNCs
groups.proposal: Place antecessive ō on a preposed supplement only in the licensed integrated structure, and keep short personal-pronominal NNCs inside a larger composition unless they are principals adjoining another constituent.
groups.writingJob: Validate the preposed subject-or-object supplement and antecessive VNC before offering integrated ō placement, enforce the short-pronominal utterance boundary, and preserve licensed cāti spelling variants without confusing graphically identical constructions.
groups.readingJob: Show why the antecessive morph belongs logically to the VNC even when written on the supplement, why the integration has no distinct English translation, and why neh or teh is a complete NNC but not an independent utterance.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses integrated or ordinary antecessive placement only when both are licensed and supplies the intended larger composition for a short pronominal NNC; the application enforces placement conditions and utterance completeness.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse composition order and a conditional antecessive-placement choice; do not add an integration toggle when the structural prerequisites are absent, and present nonsemantic spelling variants as cues.

groups.title: Marked supplementation with in
groups.proposal: Apply in to the complete adjoined unit while preserving its supplement role, topic status, reference, number, and determinacy independently.
groups.writingJob: Offer marked versus unmarked supplementation where both are licensed, attach in to the whole lower clause or sentence, preserve nested supplement roles, and project traditional demonstrative fusion without reading grammar from the fused spelling.
groups.readingJob: Show the whole-unit scope of in, the unchanged definite-indefinite and singular-plural possibilities, and the continuing subject, object, possessor, or topic role of the marked supplement.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses marked or unmarked expression when both serve the intended composition and resolves any genuinely open contextual referent reading; the application preserves the typed role and does not let in decide number or definiteness.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the optional marker and genuine referent controls; keep role, whole-unit scope, and traditional fused spelling automatic or clickable.

groups.title: Discontinuous supplementation
groups.proposal: Allow a supplement and its head to be separated by intervening constituents while preserving every typed head and recursive supplementation link.
groups.writingJob: Linearize licensed intervening clauses without breaking possessor, subject, integrated-supplement, or recursive reference edges.
groups.readingJob: Trace the separated supplement back to its head and show the nested structure instead of treating distance as loss of grammatical relation.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses constituent order when more than one licensed arrangement produces a different final composition; the application preserves all head links and derives discontinuity from that order.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse order and recursive recapture controls; do not add a discontinuous checkbox or ask the user to recreate reference links already present in the typed Results.

groups.title: Collective and named-partner agreement
groups.proposal: License collective and named-partner agreement from typed plural reference and participant identity without making visible form matching the authority.
groups.writingJob: Preserve the unresolved collective analysis where Andrews leaves it open, license apparent agreement mismatch only for a typed collective, and derive the named-partner supplement from a plural group containing the speaker or addressee plus the named third person.
groups.readingJob: Explain singular-looking collective forms, the competing moch analyses, and why only the newly identified third-person partner is spoken as the supplement.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the real participant group and selects an analysis only when the unresolved moch formula must be projected; the application derives agreement and named-partner realization from those facts.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse discourse participant and formula-analysis choices only when necessary; do not add collective or named-partner exception toggles.

groups.title: Male-bonding supplementation
groups.proposal: Derive the first-person-plural oquich-tli cross-reference only when a male speaker belongs to the referenced male group, and block it otherwise.
groups.writingJob: Use owner-issued speaker sex, group membership, oquich-tli source, and reference identity to license first-person-plural supplementation against a third-person subject or possessor head.
groups.readingJob: Show the speaker's inclusion in the male group and trace the exceptional person mismatch to each subject or possessor head.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies speaker identity and group membership because they are discourse facts; the application derives the agreement exception and ordinary oquichtin alternative.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the small discourse Source controls; do not expose male-bonding as a construction switch or infer speaker membership from the nounstem alone.

groups.title: Āyi and the silent specific-object head
groups.proposal: Keep āyi strongly transitive: realize nonspecific tla overtly, represent a specific patient with a silent object dyad, and let a supplementary object bind that silent head.
groups.writingJob: Use patient specificity to choose overt nonspecific tla or the silent specific-object head, preserve the āyi/āx stem alternation, and exclude the contrasting ichtequi pattern from this route.
groups.readingJob: Make the silently present object visible as a clickable grammatical cue and explain why an object supplement only appears headless.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies whether the intended patient is specific and, when specific, which Result identifies it; the application derives object realization, head binding, and stem form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse patient reference and supplement capture; do not add a silent-object toggle, a tla toggle, or a manual stem-form choice.

groups.title: Principal deletion and command subjects
groups.proposal: Offer licensed ca-h principal deletion as a surface transform while keeping second-person command subjects as supplementation rather than relabeling them vocatives.
groups.writingJob: Delete ca-h only when it is the shared principal of an adverbial modifier and supplementary subject, upgrade the adverbial to proxy principal, and preserve optative second-person supplements as command subjects.
groups.readingJob: Show the recoverable deleted principal and changed surface roles, and distinguish translated address-like commands from real third-person vocatives.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the full or licensed deleted composition because the final surface differs; the application validates deletion and classifies command subjects from their typed person and optative head.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse a conditional deletion choice and the normal supplementation relation; do not add a so-called-vocative choice.

groups.title: Real vocative constructions
groups.proposal: Build real vocatives from a third-person NNC and speaker context, deriving male #e or female prosody and exposing only genuinely optional surface variants.
groups.writingJob: Require a typed third-person NNC, derive speaker-conditioned realization, join and stress male #e, absorb supportive i automatically, preserve female high-tone guidance, and allow glottal-y or silent plural-in variants only in their licensed environments.
groups.readingJob: Distinguish real vocatives from second-person command subjects and explain speaker-conditioned morphology, stress, absorption, and optional variants through clickable cues.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies speaker sex and chooses among genuinely optional glottal or plural variants when more than one final surface remains licensed; the application derives all obligatory realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse vocative relation and discourse Source context; do not ask for #e, supportive-i absorption, female prosody, or third-person status after they are structurally determined.

groups.title: Free order and complete-clause structure
groups.proposal: Allow freely ordered, repeated, and recursive supplements while preserving typed roles, principal selection, and the complete-clause status of every NNC and pronominal NNC.
groups.writingJob: Linearize all licensed constituent orders, permit multiple supplements in one role and recursive supplements, and never infer role or principal from distance, markers, English translation, or word-like spelling.
groups.readingJob: Keep the organizing principal and every supplement edge visible, and remind the reader that chichi and nehhuātl remain complete assertions inside the larger sentence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses order and resolves real principal or role ambiguity only where the final composition cannot be determined; the application preserves the clause graph through every order.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse order, principal selection, head-role, and recursive recapture controls conditionally; do not add generic freedom, clause-completeness, or ambiguity switches.
